profile.headline: Robot Perception Generalist
profile.summary:
Robotics is my calling. Even though I understand the process, being able to animate inanimate objects still feels magical. It’s also a great side perk to be able to free people from having to do dull, dirty, and dangerous jobs. In this journey, I’ve been fortunate work with fantastic colleagues turned friends (and vice versa!) whether through graduate school, Willow Garage, or Mayfield Robotics.

Strategically, I’ve also gotten great mileage out of the agile startup “create an MVP first, and don’t prematurely optimize” philosophy. As robotics is foreign territory for designers, management, and other engineers, having even a duct-taped prototype often help at an organizational level to ground discussions, which helps to evolve and crispen requirements.

Skillswise, I’m a robotics generalist. I enjoy adapting mapping, planning, and machine learning algorithms for use in robots that have to operate in human spaces. And in domains where I have less expertise—as much of modern robotics share common mathematical roots—I’ve found that it takes on the order of 1-3 months to catch up to state-of-the-art (as was done with transitioning from manipulation to mapping & navigation at Mayfield Robotics).

In coding, the Zen of Python (PEP 20) is pretty near and dear to my heart. I favor simplicity and flexibility over detailed class hierarchies, which tends to often manifest as functional code. It’s a win when I can deliver functionality with less code.

Less code, less bugs.

UPDATE:
Thank you for your inquiries, but my last day at Mayfield won’t be until 10/19/2018. As us Mayfielders were rather attached to our Kuri’s, I plan to take time off for travel and professional development. This tentatively mean that I won’t be available to start interviewing until 11/05/2018.

positions.title: Senior Robotics Engineer
positions.description:
• Wrote custom SLAM stack for 2D mapping with consumer-grade depth sensors (short-ranged, noisy, less than 180 deg FOV) using Ceres, Cartographer, and libfrsm (a type of ICP scan matcher). Robustified with diverse datasets captured in real homes.
• Worked with product team to design guided flows for robot map setup, and maintenance.
• Mentored other developers on & implemented strategies for robust indoor 2D navigation (safety reflexes, recovery behaviors, docking, when/how to layer static vs. dynamic obstacles, etc).

positions.title: Robotics Engineer
positions.description:
• Setup initial infrastructure for deployment (ansible, docker, CI with Travis), and management of software configurations (drivers, kinematic/collision models, simulation environments) to work with evolving hardware prototypes.
• Created functional framework for event driven state machines & used it to write goal oriented behaviors that allowed for user interaction over multiple modalities (physical, tactile, app).

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Helped build 2 mobile manipulators (El-E, and El-E 2).
• Developed a complete pick-and-place system for home mobile manipulators where users specify which object to move and where to with a laser pointer.
• Developed a complete assistive robot system whose functions are informed by human interactions with assistive dogs.
• Developed a system where end-users program robots to perform in-home behaviors using Photoshop-like tools.
• Explored use of 3D, RFID & force torque sensors on mobile manipulators.

positions.title: Manipulation Intern
positions.description: Created ROS Commander (ROSCO) system to create behaviors for speeding up Human-in-the-Loop teleoperation built on top of RViz (a ROS 3D robot visualization package).

positions.title: Summer Intern
positions.description: Recreated a version of the laser pointer interface detector based on random forest classifiers for ROS (the Robot Operating System) that is more tolerant of extreme lighting variations introduced by sunlight (http://www.ros.org/wiki/laser_interface).
